correctness.rationale: If every operator arity is finite, each well-founded formula tree is finitely branching, hence finite by König’s lemma; quotienting worlds by agreement on its finitely many subformulas gives at most an exponential number of classes in the finite subformula count and preserves existential tuple modalities by a two-sided truth induction, including nullary operators. When some arity is infinite, ZFC supplies countably many distinct positions. The derived unary modal context yields pairwise incompatible formulas specifying exact finite path heights, one for every natural number. A single infinite-branching formula requires simultaneous witnesses for every exact-height type, forcing infinitely many worlds; explicit natural-number chains plus a root satisfy it on a countable world set. The checker independently evaluates all bounded approximations for arities 1–9; it does not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: A recent framework treats a modality’s argument positions as an arbitrary set, including infinite sets; determining which generic signatures preserve the foundational finite-model property is a natural semantic gap. The theorem supplies a complete structural boundary across all signatures: infinitely many finite-arity operators are harmless, while one infinite-arity operator destroys the property, even without propositional atoms. A transparent model construction gives the smallest possible infinite witness cardinal, and the distinction clarifies precisely when finite filtration extends to the new signature class. This is not a numerical recomputation or an arbitrary parameter slice.
